newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Issing says timely EMU start most likely scenario.
newsitem.headline: Issing says timely EMU start most likely scenario.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said a timely start to the third phase of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) on January 1, 1999 was still the most likely scenario.
Asked whether Germany's budget problems could lead to a delay to the start of a single european currency, Issing told Reuters Financial Television:
"I would not say that it is mainly Germany that causes such deliberations over delay. I think EMU will start on time. This is still the most probable (case)."

He added that not only Germany, but also other countries had a lot of work to do to live up to a strict and narrow interpretation of the Maastricht convergence criteria, as the German parliament has demanded.
